If Brand New Day is ultimately a movie about the importance of a healthy work-life balance, it doesn’t always find the right equilibrium. To begin with, its preoccupation with solitude renders it deficient in the zippy ensemble comedy that has long been the MCU’s stealthiest asset. Nor does it fully exploit Holland’s gawky charm or Zendaya’s willowy grace. To be sure, it delivers two very good scenes between Peter and MJ: one set on a rooftop against the night sky, when a seemingly cathartic kiss is revealed to be a dastardly feint; the other in a nondescript interior, where the characters’ feelings spill out in a mix of anger, hunger, and sorrow. But on the whole, the film operates as a kind of emotional placeholder, deferring any resolution or progression of its relationships to a subsequent installment.

This movie really does feel like a fresh start despite being a sequel. It feels like a new story is beginning with loose threads to the original trilogy in the best way.
The movie itself has some incredible action that is so obviously Destin Daniel Cretton's work. The camerawork in some key scenes is phenomenal.
While the script is a bit predictable and the movie's length was felt a little, it wasn't bad enough to ruin the movie for me, I'll definitely be going back an rewatching. The script and Tom Holland did incredible job's at conveying how Peter is feeling throughout the movie.

This is late but Spider man Brand new day is legit one of the best marvel movies, definitely my fav spidey movie at the moment (although nothing beats tobey for me).
